extracted.intended_audience: EPO examiners acting as ISA/IPEA and international patent applicants/agents
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for conducting international search/Chapter II preliminary examination (IPER/WO‑IPEA), handling third‑party observations, PPH requests and the required content/format of international applications submitted to the EPO as ISA/IPEA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party observations — eligibility and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Third parties may, anonymously if so desired, file observations under the PCT which ... should exclusively refer to prior art relevant to the novelty and/or inventive step of the invention claimed in the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observations are to be submitted electronically to the IB using WIPO's online tool between international publication and 28 months from the priority date. They may be filed in any language of publication and the cited prior art may be in any language. See WIPO 'ePCT Third Party Observations' guide. The applicant is notified by the IB and may file comments within 30 months from the priority date. Any third‑party observations/comments will be made available for public inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party observations — timing and transmission to Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: The IB will promptly communicate any third‑party observation and any applicant comment to the ISA, SISA and IPEA unless the (supplementary) ISR or IPER has already been received by the IB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promptly after expiration of 30 months from the priority date, observations and applicant comments are sent to all designated and elected Offices. The EPO as designated/elected Office will consider third‑party observations filed during the international phase after entry into the European phase once available to it. The EPO will make every effort to issue the next office action within three months of expiry of the Rule 161 EPC period if the third party clearly expressed that result, the observation was substantiated and not filed anonymously (applicant should indicate this in the observation or file the observation directly with EPO).

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party observations — translations and non‑EPO languages
rubrics_metrics.description: If third‑party observations and/or prior art are not in an official EPO language, the formalities officer at the EPO will invite the third party to submit a translation (with a shorter time limit within PCT deadlines), unless deadlines cannot be respected or the observation was filed anonymously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a translation is not and cannot be filed, the examiner should nevertheless take the observation into account to the extent feasible, particularly if prima facie relevant (for example, from drawings). The examiner may add a remark in the WO‑ISA that a translation will be required for detailed assessment. No invitation for translation is issued if deadlines cannot be met or the observation was anonymous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of third‑party observations in WO‑IPEA/IPER
rubrics_metrics.description: Third‑party observations received during Chapter II are taken into account when drafting the WO‑IPEA and when establishing the IPER, with specific handling depending on timing and impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a negative IPER is envisaged and a second written opinion has not been sent, a WO‑IPEA (Form 408) is drafted taking into account the applicant's comments and the third‑party observations and referring to new prior‑art documents in Section V. If a WO‑IPEA was already sent before receipt of third‑party observations and the IPER would have been negative even without them, no further written opinion is sent before establishment of the IPER. If a WO‑IPEA was sent before receipt and the IPER would have been positive without the observations, a new WO‑IPEA is issued or the applicant is called, depending on expediency (e.g., deadlines). When establishing the IPER the third‑party observations and applicant comments are taken into account and new documents referred to in Section V where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party observations — irrelevance or incomprehensibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Third‑party observations which are not relevant or not sufficiently understandable do not need to be dealt with substantially in the WO‑IPEA and/or IPER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A comment should be included in Section V of the WO‑IPEA and/or IPER indicating that the third‑party observations have been taken into account and found not to be relevant, or that they could not be taken into account and why. Observations not in an official EPO language that are unintelligible may be disregarded substantively but noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPER must not state national patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: Art. 35(2) specifies that the report shall not contain any statement on the question of whether the claimed invention is or seems to be patentable or unpatentable according to any national law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The purpose of the preliminary examination is merely to give an opinion; it does not lead to grant or refusal. The report should not give the impression that any part of the application may or may not be allowable. It will only state whether or not the claims meet certain criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPER completion — same criteria and scope as WO‑ISA; searched claims only
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPER is drafted in the same way as the WO‑ISA; a positive or negative opinion will be given for all claims, taking into account arguments/amendments submitted by the applicant. The same criteria apply as to the WO‑ISA with respect to examination issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IPER will only be established for claims which have been searched (as indicated in the WO‑ISA); any amended claims that are directed to subject‑matter not searched will not be considered and an indication will be made in Section III of the IPER (non‑establishment of opinion), with reasons on the separate sheet. See Rule 66.1(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer of prior written opinion content to IPER & neutral treatment of applicant replies
rubrics_metrics.description: If no reply has been received to a written opinion or previous objections are still valid, comments in that written opinion can be transferred to corresponding IPER sections; however, examiner should neutrally address main applicant arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if previous objections remain valid, the examiner should, in a neutral way (without direct reference like 'see reply/arguments from the applicant'), deal with at least the main arguments from the applicant to ensure the applicant knows his arguments were considered. If applicant's arguments/facts/evidence (e.g. comparative test results) are crucial to inventive step assessment, the examiner may base the IPER argumentation on the applicant's response, but must not append portions of the applicant's reply or refer directly to the applicant's letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing compliance and effect on search/examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Where no (complete) international search was carried out because the applicant did not file an electronic sequence listing conforming to WIPO Standard ST.25 or did not pay the late furnishing fee, the IPER will indicate under Section III that the examination is limited according to Rule 13ter.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IPER should also indicate the examination is limited according to Rule 66.1(e) because the search was incomplete. The applicant may be invited to furnish a compliant electronic sequence listing under Rule 13ter.1(a) and to pay the late furnishing fee under Rule 13ter.1(c) within a non‑extendable one‑month period from the date of invitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positive vs negative IPER — criteria & special non‑unitary cases
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner needs to indicate whether the IPER is to be considered positive or negative; the same criteria apply as in GL/PCT‑EPO B‑XI, 3.4 (as for WO‑ISA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a non‑unitary application special cases include: if all inventions examined are found novel and inventive but lack of unity remains the only objection, the IPER is marked negative while Section V gives positive statements on novelty/inventive step for examined inventions and unity objection is reasoned under Section IV. In such cases a negative IPER can be sent directly without a WO‑IPEA. If no additional search fees were paid and the report on the first invention is positive, the IPER is marked negative (preventing direct grant upon entry into the regional phase) and can be sent directly; Section V gives a positive statement for the first invention only and Section IV is not filled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification of IPER — grounds and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Since an IPER is a non‑binding opinion and not a decision, the PCT provides for neither opposition nor appeal against it. Only when there is an error in the IPER or the IPER has been issued when in fact a second written opinion should have been issued will rectification be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If incorrect (e.g., wrong application documents or citations, new documents cited for first time, overlooked claim amendments) and at least one week before the usual deadline (normally 28 months), a new Form 409 with correct information is completed and the corrected IPER is sent to the applicant and WIPO. If less than one week or deadline expired, the applicant is called and asked whether they wish a corrected IPER; if they decline because of the deadline, Form 428 (minutes of telephone consultation) indicating the error is completed and transmitted for information. If the applicant's request for rectification does not demonstrate defects, the formalities officer informs the applicant the international preliminary examination phase has ended and further comments may only be addressed to elected Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of demand under Chapter II — refund and formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are entitled to a refund of the whole amount of the international preliminary examination fee if the demand is withdrawn before 30 months from the priority date and provided international preliminary examination has not started.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner has actually started to examine the file, no refund will be made. The starting date is usually derived from Form PCT/IPEA/409 (Box I, point 6) indicating the date of the top‑up search. Withdrawal becomes effective upon receipt by the IB; applicants may submit withdrawal to the EPO as IPEA (EPO will mark date of receipt and promptly transmit to IB). The signature of each applicant is required if the demand is withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request to examine different sets of claims for different elected States — not accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing different sets of claims for different elected States or different (main and auxiliary) requests based on different sets of claims is not accepted under the PCT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examining multiple co‑pending requests is time‑consuming and contrary to PCT intention; auxiliary requests are not provided for. If a preferred request is clear (e.g., main request), the WO‑IPEA/IPER is established on that request with a remark that treatment of different requests is not provided under the PCT. If unclear, the applicant is asked (preferably by telephone) to furnish one set only or state which set should be used. If no reply and applicant insists on plurality, WO‑IPEA/IPER drawn up on the first set with a remark recorded under Section I.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request to examine certain claims only — not accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: A request by the applicant to establish the IPER for certain claims only (without formally restricting the set of claims) is not accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IPER is established on the claims on file and can only be restricted by the examiner (e.g., lack of unity, unsearched claims, clarity, added subject‑matter). A restriction at the applicant's request would be contrary to Art.35(2), which states the IPER relates to 'each claim'. Applicants are informed that unless a restricted set of claims is filed the IPER will be established for all claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint against findings at the search stage — procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If the search was restricted and the applicant complains about the findings at the search stage, the complaint will be dealt with by the Complaint Handling Unit at the EPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To ensure treatment as a complaint the applicant should use the online complaint form and explicitly state the reply should be considered a complaint. A substantive counterargument letter is not a complaint. While no substantive review is provided, the ISA may exceptionally issue a corrected ISR in case of a procedural flaw.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to IPER file by third parties via elected Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Provided international publication has taken place, once the IPER has been established, third parties may access the file of the international preliminary examination via those elected Offices whose national law allows access by third parties to the file of a national application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such access may be allowed to the same extent as provided by the national law for access to the file of a national application. See GL/EPO E‑IX, 2.10 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPER handling of newly cited documents that do not prejudice patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: If a positive IPER is envisaged since, even though the third‑party observations may refer to more relevant documents than the ones on file, they do not prejudice novelty and inventive step, the newly cited relevant documents are dealt with in the reasons in favour of patentability in Section V on the separate sheet as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the documents are relevant but do not add anything to what was already available, it is left to the examiner's discretion whether they need to be quoted in the IPER. For example, if the documents are a better starting point for the problem‑solution approach, the examiner may wish to review his argumentation supporting the positive assessment of inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract — purpose and examiner's role
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application must contain an abstract; the abstract merely serves the purpose of technical information and cannot be taken into account for any other purpose, particularly not for interpreting the scope of protection sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract is initially supplied by the applicant subject to exceptions; the examiner conducting international search determines its definitive content, normally published with the application. The examiner should consider the abstract in relation to the application as filed. Transmittal of the abstract content to the applicant is made with the search report (Form PCT/ISA/210, Box IV). See checklist and guidance in the Guidelines for Examination in the EPO (F‑II,2.5) and ISPE Guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title — brevity and alignment with description/claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The title must be short and precise and should first state the title of the invention as appearing in the request (Rule 5.1(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should review the title in light of the description and claims and any amendments thereto to ensure the title is concise and gives a clear and adequate indication of the subject of the invention. If amendments change claim categories, the examiner should check whether a corresponding amendment to the title is needed (may not go beyond disclosure as filed). See ISPE Guidelines for further provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description formal requirements and industrial applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: The description must meet formal requirements (use of recommended subheadings) and should indicate explicitly how the invention is capable of exploitation in industry if not obvious from the description or nature of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage of subheadings from Section 204 of the Administrative Instructions is recommended. 'Capable of exploitation in industry' means same as 'susceptible of industrial application'. Usually industrial applicability is self‑evident, but in some instances (e.g., methods of testing or certain biotechnological inventions like gene sequences) the manner of industrial exploitation must be explicitly indicated; for biotechnical sequences partial sequences, the industrial application is not self‑evident and must be disclosed in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) — eligibility and basis
rubrics_metrics.description: The PPH enables an applicant whose claims have been determined to be patentable/allowable to have a corresponding application filed with a PPH partner office processed in an accelerated manner while allowing offices to exploit available work results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the PPH pilot programme a PPH request can be based on the latest PCT work product (WO‑ISA or IPRP/IPER) established by one of the PPH partner offices as ISA or IPEA (PPH based on PCT work products), or on national work products indicating patentable/allowable claims (PPH based on national work products). Procedures/requirements for filing PPH requests are available from partner offices' websites. Irrespective of PPH, applicants may request accelerated examination under the EPO PACE programme at any time.
